samples.summary: editor.ts's new `siblingsOf` resolves cell info from the body-only `layout.blockParentMap`, so a caret inside a header/footer table cell now gets the wrong sibling array and toolbar indent/outdent silently no-ops there
samples.evidence: `recomputeLayout` computes `layout` from `doc.document.blocks` only (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1523-1533) and merges header/footer parentage into a *separate* map that it hands to the model (`doc.setBlockParentMap(mergedParentMap)`, editor.ts:1573-1580). The new `siblingsOf` (editor.ts:1618-1627, reached from the cursor-only fallback at editor.ts:1711-1712) looks the block up in `layout.blockParentMap` — the body map. For a list item inside a *header* table cell that lookup misses, so `siblingsOf` returns `doc.getContextBlocks()` (the header's top-level blocks), an array that does not contain the block. `planSiblingGroup` then finds no selected id in it and returns no changes (packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:63-83), so `applyListLevelChanges` writes nothing — where the old code indented the block unconditionally. The rest of editor.ts uses the region-inclusive map for exactly this reason (`doc.blockParentMap.get(cursor.position.blockId)`, editor.ts:4041, 4074, 4187), and text-editor.ts's equivalent helper deliberately uses the *active* layout (`getActiveLayout().blockParentMap`, packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3650-3655), which is why the header case works on the Tab / Cmd+] path but not on the toolbar path. Fix belongs on the new code: use `doc.blockParentMap` (or the active-region layout) in `siblingsOf`. Header/footer table cells are a supported caret location per the comment at editor.ts:1568-1572; the added tests cover header lists and body-table lists but never a header-table cell.

samples.summary: The list-level ceiling is now centralized as `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` in packages/docs, but slides still hardcodes/omits it, so the constant that now gates the new subtree refusal can drift from the values slides produces
samples.evidence: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:85 still hardcodes the ceiling (`return ` lvl="${Math.min(8, n)}"`), and packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:268 assigns `block.listLevel = list.level` with no clamp at all. Slides mounts the docs text-box editor (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:446, `indent()` delegating at :641-645), whose indent boundary is now `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` from packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:7. A pptx-imported deck can therefore hold levels above the shared ceiling, and any future change to `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` will not reach either slides site. These call sites still work today; they are out of step with the new single source of truth.

verdict.reason: Every claimed fact checks out. `recomputeLayout` computes `layout` from `doc.document.blocks` only (editor.ts:1523-1533) and merges header/footer parentage into a separate map given to the model (editor.ts:1573-1580), while the new `siblingsOf` (editor.ts:1618-1627) is fed `layout.blockParentMap.get(block.id)` from the cursor-only fallback (editor.ts:1711-1712). For a list item inside a header/footer table cell that lookup misses, so `siblingsOf` returns `doc.getContextBlocks()` — the header's top-level blocks (document.ts:158-162) — which does not contain the block. `planSiblingGroup` only emits changes for ids present in the passed array (list-level.ts:64-83), so `applyListLevelChanges` (editor.ts:1595-1612) writes nothing, and `indent()`/`outdent()`'s marginLeft pass early-returns for list items (editor.ts:3578-3583, 3594-3601) — a silent no-op. The path is reachable from out-of-diff consumers: the docs toolbar calls the exported API's `indent`/`outdent` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:949-953; text-paragraph-group.tsx:212,230), and those API methods contain no header-context delegation. The keyboard equivalent deliberately uses the active layout (text-editor.ts:2870-2879 via getCellInfo at 3650-3655), and the rest of editor.ts uses the region-inclusive `doc.blockParentMap` (editor.ts:4041,4072,4074), confirming the intended contract. Not guarded, not out of scope: a behaviour break at cross-package consumers of an exported symbol on a supported caret location.

mergedFrom.summary: `TextEditor.siblingsOf` returns the body-only `doc.document.blocks`, ignoring the header/footer edit context, so Tab / Shift+Tab / Cmd+] on a list item while editing a header or footer now plans no change at all (silent no-op where it previously worked).

finding.summary: `siblingsOf` was made context-aware, but the selection branch of `forEachBlockInSelection` still indexes `doc.document.blocks` with context-relative indices — Tab/indent in a header/footer with a multi-block selection mutates body blocks or throws
finding.evidence: The delta fixes only the cursor-only fallback (text-editor.ts:2869 `return this.doc.getContextBlocks()`). The selection branch bypasses `siblingsOf` entirely: `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2831-2849` computes `startIdx/endIdx` with `this.doc.getBlockIndex(...)`, which resolves against `getContextBlocks()` (`packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:272` → `document.ts:158-161`, header/footer array when `doc.editContext !== 'body'`, set at `text-editor.ts:405`), then walks `const topLevel = this.doc.document.blocks` (line 2836) and calls `fn(b, topLevel)` (line 2849). With the caret in a header/footer and a range spanning two blocks, `applyListLevelChanges` (line 2712) therefore rewrites *body* blocks' `listLevel` (and `handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` at 2754/2768 their `marginLeft`); if the header/footer region has more blocks than the body, `topLevel[i]` is `undefined` and `b.type` throws inside the keydown handler. The sibling implementation in `editor.ts` already does this correctly — `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1689-1702` uses `doc.getContextBlocks()` for the same branch — so text-editor.ts is now the only inconsistent copy. The new test (`editor-tab-bullet.test.ts:333-373`) exercises only the cursor-only path, so nothing catches this. Fix belongs at text-editor.ts:2836 (use `getContextBlocks()`).

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. The finding claims text-editor.ts:2836 assigns `const topLevel = this.doc.document.blocks` and line 2849 calls `fn(b, topLevel)`. In the working tree, the multi-block selection branch of `forEachBlockInSelection` instead does `const contextBlocks = this.doc.getContextBlocks();` (text-editor.ts:2843), iterates `contextBlocks[i]` (2845), and passes `fn(b, contextBlocks)` (2856). A Grep for `topLevel` in text-editor.ts returns no hits; `document.blocks` appears in that region only inside an explanatory comment at 2836 and 2872 that names this exact hazard. Because `getBlockIndex` (model/document.ts:271-273) resolves via `getContextBlocks()` (document.ts:158-162), and the walked array is now that same context container, the indices and the array agree: a header/footer multi-block selection visits header/footer blocks, so neither the body-block listLevel/marginLeft mutation nor the `undefined`/`b.type` throw is reachable on this path. The branch is also structurally identical to editor.ts:1689-1702, which the finding itself cites as the correct implementation, so the claimed inconsistency between the two copies does not exist. The fix the finding prescribes for text-editor.ts:2836 is already the code that is there.
